newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos checks out of hospital.
newsitem.headline: Ramos checks out of hospital.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos, seeking to dispell reports he had suffered a stroke, danced with nurses at a Christmas party before checking out of a hospital on Sunday after two days of tests, his office said.
"Back to work," an aide quoted Ramos as saying as he left Manila's Makati Medical Centre after being treated for what doctors said was a throat infection.

Ramos, a 68-year-old workaholic, was admitted to the hospital on Thursday night. He checked himself out on Friday to host a dinner for Prince Henri of Luxembourg and returned to the hospital on Friday evening for further tests and treatment.
Several Manila newspapers reported he had suffered a mild stroke.
Hospital medical director Raul Fores denied the reports and said Ramos only suffered from a throat infection. But Fores said the president needed to slow down.
"He is not young anymore," the doctor said.
Ramos told reporters he thought he had the flu.

On the eve of his leaving the hospital, Ramos attended a Christmas party at the hospital, ate all the food served to him, danced a fast number with First Lady Amelita Ramos and then the cha cha with nurses, a Presidential Palace news release said.
His official schedule for Monday lists a heavy day of speaking engagements, several meetings and a news interview.

Ramos' admission to hospital coincided with a raging controversy over moves by a citizens group to seek an amendment to the constitution allowing him to run for re-election when his six-year term ends in June 1998.
The constitution limits a president to a single term.
